history.summary: PROVISIONAL RECORD: no web source documents any Shiva temple at or near Khuga Dam - its name, location, founding date and management are all unpublished and marked (verify) throughout this record. What is verifiable is the Khuga Dam context. Khuga Dam (also called Tuitha Dam) is a multipurpose dam on the Khuga/Tuitha River south of Churachandpur town, near Mata village, in Churachandpur district, Manipur: construction started in 1983, resumed in 2002 after a long standstill, and it was inaugurated on November 12, 2010 by Sonia Gandhi (Wikipedia). It is about 38 m high and 230 m wide and cost ~INR 2.5 billion; per Wikipedia the irrigation canal is functional only a few kilometres downstream and the planned hydroelectric generation never materialised (no power house as of 2021). The dam/reservoir area is a calm picnic/landscape viewpoint about 12 km south of Churachandpur town (meta.ai place listing pins the viewpoint at 24.238374, 93.723344). CSV TOWN FLAG: 'Churachandpur' is approximate - the dam itself is south of the town near Mata village. A Shiva shrine associated with the dam area may exist, but nothing about it could be confirmed online; it may also be a conflation of the dam with a nearby shrine (verify before use). Coordinates below are the dam's Wikipedia coordinates, not the shrine's. No reliable image found (media empty).

town_description: Churachandpur (locally called Lamka) is the second-largest town of Manipur and the headquarters of Churachandpur district, about 60 km southwest of Imphal on Tiddim Road. It is the heartland of the Kuki-Chin hill tribes (Thadou-Kuki, Hmar, Paite, Zou) and is overwhelmingly Christian; a small Hindu/Meitei community maintains shrines in and around the town. Khuga Dam, on the Khuga (Tuitha) River near Mata village about 12 km south of town, is the district's main reservoir and picnic viewpoint.
